transcript.text: Hello, I'm Commander Gary Cuso of the Santa Ana Police Department.
What you are about to view is a critical incident community video briefing of an officer-involved shooting that occurred on Wednesday, January 28, 2026.
In the event of a critical incident, we strive to disseminate as much information as possible at the earliest opportunity, contingent upon the progress of the investigation.
These briefings are intended to provide the public with open and transparent communication
regarding officer-involved critical incidents.
The information presented is based on the facts known at the time of the video briefing.
Critical incidents are often high-stress and emotional for those involved.
As a result of this stress and emotion, audio and video recordings may contain strong language
and digital images may be graphic.
Some viewers may find these videos disturbing and unsuitable for children.
Good evening, I am Officer Natalie Garcia, the Public Information Officer for the Santa Ana Police Department.
I will provide you with a brief overview of an officer-involved shooting that occurred on January 28, 2026.

At approximately 1029 p a Santa Police officer attempted to stop a vehicle that was speeding in the area of Santa Ana Boulevard and French Street The vehicle failed to yield and a slow vehicle pursuit ensued The driver continued
for several blocks, running red lights, until eventually entering the parking structure located
at 450 East 4th Street. The driver quickly sped into a parking structure and collided with an
object inside. When the vehicle stopped, the male driver exited and dropped a firearm. He then walked
toward the officer with his hands up. Despite repeated commands to get on the
ground, the male continued advancing towards the officer. The officer issued
additional commands to keep his hands up in an effort to de-escalate the
situation. The male then turned and walked back towards the firearm. The
officer repeatedly ordered him not to reach for the firearm, but he failed to
comply, at which an officer-involved shooting occurred. The male was struck by
gunfire. Officers rendered medical aid until Orange County Fire Authority arrived and continued
life-saving measures. The subject was ultimately pronounced deceased at the scene. First, you
will see and hear select segments from officers' body-worn camera, followed by surveillance
footage from inside the parking structure and video recorded by a citizen that was posted
online. It is important to note that body-worn camera footage can be obscured by objects,

When an officer-involved shooting occurs, multiple investigations are automatically
initiated.
The Orange County District Attorney's Office conducts an independent investigation into
any potential criminal conduct by the involved officers.
Additionally, the Santa Ana Police Department's Crimes Against Persons Division investigates
any alleged criminal conduct by the suspect.
This comprehensive review examines both Lopez's action and the officer involved in the shooting.
The investigation remains active and ongoing.
As with all officer-involved shootings, the incident will ultimately be reviewed by the District Attorney's Office.
Separately, the Department's Internal Affairs Division conducts an internal administrative review to evaluate the officer's actions for compliance with policy and training standards.
We take every use of force seriously and make every effort to de-escalate situations whenever possible.
